blocks.content: DNH&DD's economy shows a striking internal contrast that is a favourite exam theme: Dadra & Nagar Haveli is one of India's most industrialised small territories (a major manufacturing hub), while Daman and Diu lean more towards trade, fishing, tourism and — historically — a liquor-trade economy linked to their former Portuguese-territory status.
Industrial Profile of Dadra & Nagar Haveli

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Dadra & Nagar Haveli's economy relies heavily on manufacturing industries, notably textiles, plastics, electronics, and pharmaceuticals, with Silvassa as its main industrial hub.
Daman and Diu's economy is primarily driven by tourism, fisheries, pharmaceuticals, distilleries, and coastal commercial activities.
The official merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu into a single Union Territory took effect on 26th January 2020.
Strategic proximity to NH-48 and major industrial corridors in Gujarat and Maharashtra significantly enhances the region's connectivity and economic output.

blocks.content: Dadra & Nagar Haveli has developed into a significant small-and-medium industrial hub since the 1970s–80s, driven by tax incentives, proximity to the Mumbai–Ahmedabad industrial corridor, and cheap land and labour — industrial estates around Silvassa host units in engineering, plastics, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, textiles and electronics.
The economic landscape of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu is characterized by rapid manufacturing growth, strong connectivity, and thriving coastal tourism.

Because of this industrial base, DNH&DD (led by Dadra & Nagar Haveli) has consistently ranked among the highest Indian states/UTs by per-capita industrial output and has attracted substantial small-scale and medium-scale manufacturing investment relative to its tiny size — a frequently cited comparative economic fact.
Key industrial estates include those at Silvassa, Masat, Khadoli and Piparia, developed and managed with support from the UT Administration's Industries Department.

cells: Engineering goods, plastics & PVC products, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles, electronics, food processing
Tax/duty incentives, proximity to Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor and Vapi (Gujarat), lower land/labour costs
Paddy, ragi (finger millet), pulses — largely tribal, small-holder subsistence farming supplemented by forest produce

rows: Heavy & Light Manufacturing, Textiles, Plastics, Engineering

items: Fishing is a traditional mainstay of both Daman and Diu, given their coastal location — Daman's fishing harbour and Diu's fishing fleet support a substantial local seafood trade and export activity.

Tourism (beaches, Portuguese-era forts and churches, and — historically — comparatively liberal liquor laws inherited from the pre-merger Daman & Diu UT) drives significant footfall, especially from neighbouring 'dry' Gujarat, where alcohol sales are prohibited under state Prohibition law.

Small-scale industry (textiles, food processing) exists in Daman but on a much smaller scale than Dadra & Nagar Haveli's manufacturing base; Diu's economy remains the smallest and most tourism/fishing-dependent of the three districts.

Salt production (from coastal salt pans) has historically been practised in parts of the Daman and Diu coastline, alongside small-scale boat-building and net-making trades tied to the fishing economy.
Silvassa is widely tested as the primary industrial hub of Dadra & Nagar Haveli, famous for high-density industrial estates.
Remember the merger date (26th January 2020) enacted via the Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019.
Diu features direct air connectivity via Diu Airport, crucial for regional tourism and trade questions in competitive exams.
Diu Airport connects the island to Mumbai and other cities; Daman lacks its own commercial airport and is served via road/rail from Vapi (Gujarat) and Mumbai.
The Western Railway line passes through Vapi, the nearest major railhead to both Dadra & Nagar Haveli (Silvassa) and Daman, linking the territory to the Mumbai–Ahmedabad–Delhi trunk route.

NAMO Medical Education and Research Institute, Silvassa — a flagship medical college and hospital complex inaugurated in recent years, is a notable healthcare/education infrastructure landmark for the UT, visited by the President and Vice-President during official tours (Nov/Sept 2024).
Dadra & Nagar Haveli = a major small-scale/medium industrial hub (engineering, plastics, pharma, chemicals) — punches above its size in per-capita industrial output.
Daman & Diu = fishing- and tourism-driven; Daman's liberal liquor sale (a legacy of its pre-merger status) draws visitors from neighbouring 'dry' Gujarat.
Key industrial estates: Silvassa, Masat, Khadoli, Piparia.
Diu has its own airport; Daman and Dadra & Nagar Haveli rely on Vapi (Gujarat) for rail connectivity.
NAMO Medical Education and Research Institute, Silvassa, is a key recent healthcare/education landmark.
